Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

peace noun

peace and quiet

also peace and quiet, calm, tranquillity, tranquility, leave me in peace

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.2
Ov. Met. 11.623

quiēs, quiētis f.

noun, third declension

rest, quiet, peace

Rest from work and from cares (Lewis & Short); the noun of quiēscere.

Other words

  • ōtium, ōtiī n. — leisure, time free of business; peace and quiet

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Agr. 2.102: pāx, tranquillitās, ōtium (Lewis & Short)

    The opposite of negōtium.

  • tranquillitās, tranquillitātis f. — calm, tranquillity

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.2; Cic. Agr. 2.102 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • nam quī locus quiētis et tranquillitātis plēnissimus fore vidēbātur, in eō maximae mōlēs molestiārum et turbulentissimae tempestātēs exstitērunt

    for the very time of life that looked like being fullest of peace and quiet brought the greatest mass of troubles and the wildest stormsCic. de Or. 1.2

  • Somne, quiēs rērum, placidissime, Somne, deōrum, pāx animī, quem cūra fugit

    Sleep, rest of all things, gentlest of the gods, Sleep, peace of the mind, from whom care fleesOv. Met. 11.623–624

See also peace, rest, quiet!.
